title: Emoji Mood Tracker
story: You're building a mood journal app. Instead of typing "I feel happy today," users pick a mood from a list, and the app shows a matching emoji. An enum with a custom method makes this intuitive.
why: Enum methods let each variant carry its own behavior � each mood knows its own emoji.
analogy: An enum method is like asking each variant a question: "What's your emoji?" Happy answers with a smile, Sad answers with a frown. Each variant has its own answer.
try_it: Add three more moods: Anxious, Calm, and Grumpy. Give each an emoji, a label, and an energy level. Create a function that takes two moods and returns the one with higher energy.
tips: Method signatures use `fn TypeName.method(self)` � the type comes before the dot
Inside a method, use `match self` to branch on which variant the instance holds
Match arms must be exhaustive � every variant needs an arm (the compiler checks this)
common_mistakes: Forgetting a variant in `match` � the compiler will tell you which ones are missing
Using ellipsis `...` or `_` in match without understanding it matches ALL remaining variants
